concept.body: To divide the segment from A to B in the ratio m : n (measured from A), walk the fraction k = m/(m + n) of the displacement: P = A + k(B − A), coordinate by coordinate. Similar triangles make the coordinate fraction equal the length fraction. Swapping which endpoint leads mirrors the point.

explanationVariants: One fifth of the run: x = 2.

widget.prompt: P divides the segment from (0, 0) to (10, 5) in the ratio 1 : 4. Enter P's x-coordinate.

commonErrors.feedback: 5 is the midpoint's x — 1:4 walks only k = 1/5: x = 2.
8 rides k = 4/5, the swapped ratio — from the origin, 1:4 stops at x = 2.

steps.body: The midpoint splits a segment 1 : 1 — but any ratio is buyable. To divide AB in the ratio **m : n from A**, walk the fraction k = m/(m + n) of the way: **P = A + k(B − A)**, applied to each coordinate. For 2 : 1, k = 2/3: two parts down, one to go.

widget.prompt: P divides the segment from A(1, 1) to B(7, 10) in the ratio 2 : 1. Enter P's x-coordinate.

commonErrors.feedback: 4 is the MIDPOINT's x ((1+7)/2) — the 1:1 split. A 2:1 split walks k = 2/3 of the run: 1 + 4 = 5.
3 walks only k = 1/3 — the SWAPPED ratio 1:2. From A, 2:1 means two parts first: k = 2/3, x = 5.
7 is B's own x — the full walk. Stop at two thirds: 1 + (2/3)(6) = 5.

steps.body: Why does the coordinate walk match the geometric ratio? **Similar triangles** again: the run-rise triangle from A to P is a k-scaled copy of the full A-to-B triangle, so AP is k of AB along the segment itself — the same 1/2-argument that justified the midpoint, generalized to any k. Direction matters: the ratio counts **from the first-named point**.

widget.prompt: P divides the segment from A(2, 0) to B(10, 8) in the ratio 1 : 3. Enter P's x-coordinate.

commonErrors.feedback: 6 is the midpoint's x — 1:3 is an UNEVEN split: k = 1/4, so x = 2 + 2 = 4.
8 walks k = 3/4 — the swapped ratio 3:1. From A, 1:3 puts the SHORT piece first: x = 4.
10 is B — the walk stops at a quarter: 2 + (1/4)(8) = 4.

explanationVariants: From B, the 1:3 walk uses k = 1/4 of the REVERSED displacement: 10 + (1/4)(2 − 10) = 8.

widget.prompt: Same segment, but now P divides it 1 : 3 measured FROM B. Where does P land?

options.label: (8, 6) — a quarter of the way from B toward A
options.feedback: The ratio reads from its first-named endpoint: 10 + (1/4)(−8) = 8 and 8 + (1/4)(−8) = 6. Direction is half the definition.

options.label: (4, 2), the same point as before
options.feedback: Swapping the start moves the point — 1:3 from B mirrors 3:1 from A, landing at (8, 6).

options.label: (6, 4), the midpoint
options.feedback: Only 1:1 lands at the midpoint — this uneven split sits a quarter from B: (8, 6).

options.label: The ratio can't be measured from B
options.feedback: Any endpoint can lead — the formula just uses that endpoint as A: P = B + (1/4)(A − B) = (8, 6).

widget.prompt: P(3, 4) sits on the segment from A(1, 1) to B(7, 10). P divides AB in the ratio m : n from A with m + n smallest. Enter m.

commonErrors.feedback: 2 would put P two parts along (at (5, 7)) — here the walk is (3−1)/(7−1) = 1/3, so the ratio is 1 : 2, m = 1.
3 counts the total parts — the ratio 1 : 2 has m = 1 (one part taken, two remaining).

widget.fallbackFeedback: k = 2/6 = 1/3 ⇒ ratio 1 : 2 from A ⇒ m = 1. (The y-lane agrees: 3/9 = 1/3 ✓.)

widget.prompt: A trail runs straight from the lodge (0, 2) to the summit (12, 10). A water station sits 3 : 1 of the way up (from the lodge). Enter the station's x-coordinate.

commonErrors.feedback: 3 walks k = 1/4 — the swapped ratio. Three parts of four from the lodge: (3/4)(12) = 9.
6 is halfway — 3:1 rides three quarters: x = 9.

hints: Trisection points divide AB in ratios 1:2 and 2:1 from A.
Compute both with k = 1/3 and k = 2/3 on the displacement (9, −6).
The question wants the point NEARER B — which k is that?
explanationVariants: Nearer B means the LONGER walk: k = 2/3. P = (−1 + 6, 5 − 4) = (5, 1). Enter 5.

widget.prompt: Segment from A(−1, 5) to B(8, −1) is trisected. Enter the x-coordinate of the trisection point NEARER TO B.

commonErrors.feedback: 2 is the k = 1/3 point (nearer A) — nearer B rides k = 2/3: −1 + 6 = 5.
3.5 is the MIDPOINT's x — trisection points sit at thirds, and the B-side one is at x = 5.
8 is B itself — the trisection point stops a third short: x = 5.

takeaways: P = A + k(B − A) with k = m/(m + n) — the m : n point measured FROM A.
Similar triangles guarantee the coordinate walk matches the segment ratio.
Direction is part of the ratio; midpoints are the k = 1/2 special case.
